h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ב Pesach — Maamar Lamed Bais

p: "He made a remembrance for His wonders;
This refers to our mentioning the Exodus
for one must mention the Splitting of the Sea
and the plague of the firstborn
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק א' הֲלָכָה ו', וּבִשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"ב, ג').
for the Splitting of the Sea depends on Atika,
as brought in the holy Zohar
and it is the supernal Wonder.
And likewise the plague of the firstborn,
for they left the kelipah from the tenth attribute,
which is "the first of the nations,"
at the tenth attribute counting from below upward,
שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, פֶּלֶא עֶלְיוֹן.
which is the attribute of Kesser Elyon, the supernal Wonder.
And this is "He made a remembrance for His wonders."
And the reason Hashem, may He be blessed, commanded
to remember the two wonders mentioned
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַזִּכָּרוֹן יוּכְלוּ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ אָז
through the remembrance one can then draw down
that they merit the holiness of Atika, the Wonder.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
And as we find with Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa
who said: "He Who said to oil that it should burn
will say to vinegar that it should burn."
"He Who said to oil that it should burn"?
that Hashem, may He be blessed, so imprinted
in the nature of oil that it burns,
and through this one can draw down
that He say to vinegar that it should burn.
And in the manner of what I heard
מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
from our holy Rebbe, of blessed memory, for life in the World to Come,
who said: what we find with Elisha
"And he cut off a stick and threw it there,
why did he need to cut a stick and throw it?
Only because he wished to recall
that Hashem, may He be blessed, imprinted in wood
that it floats on the surface of the water,
and through this he threw it,
שֶׁיִּתֵּן ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ טֶבַע זוֹ גַּם בַּבַּרְזֶל.
so that Hashem, may He be blessed, would put this nature in iron as well.
Elisha did this with an action,
וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא זָכַר זֶה בַּפֶּה:
and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa recalled it with his mouth:
"He Who said to oil that it should burn," etc.
וְאֶצְלוֹ לֹא הָיָה זֶה מַעֲשֵׂה נִסִּים,
And for him this was not a miraculous act,
for then he certainly would not have wanted
רַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָיָה בָּרוּר לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו
rather, since it was clear before his eyes
that there is no nature or habit at all,
רַק מַה שֶּׁה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ נוֹתֵן בָּזֶה הַטֶּבַע,
only what Hashem, may He be blessed, places as this nature,
it appeared the same to him
as if vinegar were to burn.
And by recalling with his mouth
"He Who said to oil that it should burn" —
that this is only by the word of Hashem, may He be blessed —
through this he drew down the flow
And this is "He made a remembrance for His wonders";
the reason is "gracious and merciful is Hashem,"
for through the remembrance one can draw down
the flow from Atika, which is the Wonder.
"He gave food to those who fear Him."
But Hashem, may He be blessed, feeds and sustains
Rather it refers to the eating of matzah,
which is an eating of mitzvah in holiness,
"Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us";
and it is without leaven and chametz,
that is, that there be found in it
which comes from the serpent having put
and this only "those who fear Him" merit.
that is, it will benefit the whole year,
as brought in the holy Zohar
the fruit of the Table from Shabbos to Shabbos," etc.,
so that the evil inclination should not accuse through them,
דְּהָא יֵצֶר הָרַע לָא אִשְׁתְּכַח וְכוּלֵּי.
for the evil inclination was not found," etc.
that the Kohanim ate on Shabbos
benefited all their eating on weekdays,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרַע,
that it have no accusation of the evil inclination,
which is without "the leaven in the dough,"
benefits the eating of the whole year,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בָּהֶם קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרַע,
with no accusation of the evil inclination,
which is "the leaven in the dough."
And this is "He will remember His covenant forever":
that it will be for all eternity.
And likewise Torah and circumcision are called "covenant,"
for it too is for all eternity;
for the Torah was given as a gift to Israel,
to the point that they said "It is not in Heaven."
one who is circumcised is called a tzaddik,
nevertheless "and Your people are all righteous,"
as brought in the holy Zohar
And likewise Shabbos is called a "sign of the covenant,"
and likewise eating matzah benefits forever,
"The strength of His works He told to His people,
to give them the inheritance of the nations."
And in all the nations there is wisdom,
"And You give life to them all,"
"Wisdom gives life to those who have it";
the essence of life is wisdom.
And there are found in the nations of the world
telling is in the secret of wisdom,
And this is why He scattered Israel
"so that converts be added to them";
and they explained that this means the holy sparks
and as a consequence it follows
And this is what is said:
"to give them the inheritance of the nations" —
the life and wisdom within them.
שֶׁכֵּן עִיקַּר הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
For indeed the main spread of the Oral Torah
"Ezra came up from Babylon and established it," etc.,
And likewise the purpose of all the exiles
is to bring out the Oral Torah
that is among the nations of the world.
And a person does not know
what he will receive from them of the holy sparks;
and about this it is said "He told to His people":
for Hashem, may He be blessed, draws down, in the secret of wisdom,
the words of Torah into a person's heart,
to bring out the holy sparks according to the generation.
And Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant;
the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos;
וְיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and the seventh day is the Oral Torah
and Malchus is the mouth, the Oral Torah.
much is the time to bring out

paragraphs.text: Ta'anis 25a — R. Chanina ben Dosa's daughter had lit the Shabbos lamp with vinegar instead of oil. "He said to her: My daughter, what does it matter to you? He who told oil to burn will tell vinegar to burn." It burned all day until they took light from it for Havdalah. Rashi: they lit another lamp from it and extinguished the miraculous one.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Simchas Torah 15 — “All the prophets had to raise the thing in which they wished to work a wonder above the nature of this world, as with Elisha: ‘Bring flour, and he cast it into the pot’; that is, He who set nature in the world that flour be food will say also to the wild gourd that it be food. And: ‘He cut off a stick… and the iron floated’: He who said to wood that it float will say to iron that it float. But to show the wonder within this world’s nature, without rising above it, was not possible for them.” Connection: It reads Elisha’s stick exactly as here, and adds that Moshe and Yeshayahu, unlike the other prophets, worked wonders within nature itself without first lifting the thing above it.

paragraphs.text: Ta'anis 24b — when angels in the form of sailors filled boats with sand that turned to fine flour, Rav Yehudah said: "Do not buy from this, for it is the product of a miracle." Rashi: wherever one can keep away from the product of a miracle, it is better and proper.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Taanis 25a — “Our Sages said that if a miracle is done for a person, it is deducted from his merits. It is also known that the Name Havayah acts above nature, and from its side there is no difference between a natural thing and an unnatural one; only the Name Elokim acts through nature, and therefore Elokim equals ‘ha-teva,’ nature, in numerical value. For righteous people whom Hashem conducts through the Name Havayah, constant miracles deduct nothing, for there nature and non-nature are alike, and for them it is an ordinary thing. So he told her: ‘He Who said to oil that it should burn will say to vinegar that it should burn,’ for vinegar burning is, for us, like oil burning.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada likewise explains why this was no miracle for R. Chanina ben Dosa: for him there was no nature apart from the Divine word; he adds the distinction between the Names Havayah and Elokim.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 154a–b (Terumah) — "The kohanim would gather the 'fruit' of the Table from Shabbos to Shabbos, to show that supernal sustenance goes out from that Table. Through the bread the kohanim gathered, all the food people ate and drank was blessed, so that the evil inclination would not accuse them, for it is found only amid eating and drinking."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Es HaOchel 10 — “‘The leaven in the dough’: the root of the evil inclination is in eating, from the root of the serpent, and the Sages said the Tree of Knowledge was wheat. Against it, eating matzah gives holiness to all the foods of bread of the whole year, eating maror to all foods of vegetables, and eating sacred offerings to meat. Therefore nowadays an unlearned man is forbidden to eat meat, for we have no eating of meat over which we bless ‘who sanctified us with His commandments,’ except Torah scholars, who need not sanctify their bodies, for they themselves are holy.” Connection: It gives the same claim, that matzah hallows the year’s bread, and adds that maror and the offerings do the same for vegetables and meat.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 32a — "Great is milah, for were it not for milah, heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, 'If not for My covenant day and night…'" And R. Elazar: "Great is Torah, for were it not for Torah heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, 'If not for My covenant…'" Rashi: one applies the verse to milah, the other to Torah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 93a (Lech Lecha) — "'Your people are all righteous'… are all Israel righteous? There are so many sinners and wicked in Israel! Rather… when they are circumcised they enter the good portion of the Holy One, as it is written, 'and the righteous is the foundation of the world'; and since they have entered this portion of the Tzaddik, they are called righteous — surely 'all of them righteous.'"
